topic.name: Calculating the Number of Terms in an Arithmetic Series

question.text: An arithmetic series has the first term $a_{1}=4$, the $8$th term $a_{8}=60$, and the sum of the series is $S_N=1600.$ Find the number of terms $N$ in the series.
question.explanation:
To solve this problem, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series.

\[ S_N = \dfrac N 2 \big( 2a_1 + (N-1) d \big) \]

Since we know two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference, as follows:

\begin{align*} d &= \dfrac{a_{8}-a_{1}}{8-1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{60-4}{8-1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{56}{7} \\[5pt] &= 8 \end{align*}

Now, substituting $a_1=4$, $d=8$, and $S_N=1600$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have:

\begin{align*} S_N &= \dfrac N 2 \big( 2a_1 + (N-1) d \big) \\[5pt] 1600 &= \dfrac N 2 \big( 2 \cdot 4 + (N-1) \cdot 8 \big) \\[5pt] 1600 & = \dfrac N 2 (8+ 8N - 8) \\[5pt] 1600 & = \dfrac N 2 (8N) \\[5pt] 1600 & = 4 N^2 \\[3pt] 400 & = N^2 \\[3pt] N & = 20 \end{align*}

Notice that we take the positive square root because $N$ can't be negative.

example.title: Calculating the Number of Terms in an Arithmetic Series Given Two Terms and the Sum

question.text: Calculate the number of terms in the following arithmetic series. \[ 3+9+15+\ldots =300 \]
question.explanation:
To solve this problem, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series:

\[ S_{N} = \dfrac{N}{2} \big( 2a_1+(N-1)d \big) \\[3pt] \]

We have been given the sum $S_N = 300$, and the first term $a_1=3.$ Our goal is to find $N,$ the number of terms.

The common difference $d$ can be found, as follows:

\begin{align*} d &= a_2 - a_1 \\[3pt] &= 9 - 3 \\[3pt] &= 6 \end{align*}

Substituting these values into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have:

\begin{align*} S_{N} &= \dfrac{N}{2} \big( 2a_1+(N-1)d \big) \\[5pt] 300 &= \dfrac{N}{2}(2\cdot 3+(N-1)\cdot 6) \\[5pt] 300 &= \dfrac{N}{2}(6+6N-6) \\[5pt] 300 &= \dfrac{N}{2}(6N) \\[5pt] 300 &=3N^2 \\[3pt] 100 &=N^2 \\[3pt] N &= 10 \end{align*}

Notice that we take the positive square root because $N$can't be negative. Therefore, our series has $N=10$ terms.

example.title: Calculating the Number of Terms in an Arithmetic Series Given the Pattern and the Sum

question.text: Calculate the number of terms in the following arithmetic series. \[ 5+15+25+\ldots =180 \]
question.explanation:
To solve this problem, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series:

\[ S_{N} = \dfrac{N}{2} \big( 2a_1+(N-1)d \big) \\[3pt] \]

We have been given the sum $S_N = 180$, and the first term $a_1=5.$ Our goal is to find $N,$ the number of terms.

The common difference $d$ can be found, as follows:

\begin{align*} d &= a_2 - a_1 \\[3pt] &= 15 - 5 \\[3pt] &= 10 \end{align*}

Substituting these values into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have:

\begin{align*} S_{N} &= \dfrac{N}{2} \big( 2a_1+(N-1)d \big) \\[5pt] 180 &= \dfrac{N}{2}(2\cdot 5+(N-1)\cdot 10) \\[5pt] 180 &= \dfrac{N}{2}(10+10N-10) \\[5pt] 180 &= \dfrac{N}{2}(10N) \\[5pt] 180 &=5N^2 \\[3pt] 36 &=N^2 \\[3pt] N &= 6 \end{align*}

Notice that we take the positive square root because $N$can't be negative. Therefore, our series has $N=6$ terms.
